Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.lead: Encore was designed to handle as little data as possible, and almost everything happens on your own device. This page explains what is processed, where, for how long and how to revoke access.
summary: The history you upload never leaves your browser: nothing is uploaded to a server.
We have no database, no accounts of our own, no analytics and no tracking cookies.
In Connect mode, we only keep your Spotify access in an encrypted cookie in your browser.

what.title: What is processed
what.upload: From the extended history file we only read: date and time of each play, how long it played, the track, artist and album names, the track identifier, the platform (phone, computer…) and whether it was skipped or played on shuffle.
what.uploadDiscarded: IP address, connection country and the other fields in the file are discarded while reading and never used.
what.connect: With your authorization, we read your basic profile (identifier, name and photo), your tops, recently played and liked tracks. The requested permissions are read-only.
what.demo: Uses only made-up data, generated in your browser. No personal data is processed.

where.title: Where the data lives
where.body: Your file is processed in a Web Worker in your browser. In Connect mode, the Encore server only relays requests to Spotify and returns a reduced version of the response, without storing it. The site is hosted on Vercel.

howLong.title: For how long
items: Uploaded history: only in the tab's memory, until you reload or close the page.
Spotify responses (Connect): in the tab's memory or sessionStorage, for at most 12 hours, and cleared when you sign out.
Session cookie (Connect): encrypted, lasts at most 30 days and is deleted when you click Sign out.
Server technical logs: only route, status and duration of requests, with no content, kept by the provider for about 1 hour.

legal.title: Legal basis
legal.body: Processing is needed to provide the service you asked for (Brazil's LGPD, art. 7, V). We don't use your data for advertising or profiling, and we don't share it with third parties.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.body: We don't sell or share data. Spotify is the source of Connect mode data, and Vercel hosts the site. Cards you create stay on your device until you choose to share them.

rights.title: Your rights and how to revoke
items: Delete the uploaded history: close or reload the tab.
End Connect mode: use the Sign out button, which deletes the cookie and this tab's cache.
Revoke Encore's access to your account: remove the app at
rights.contact: Questions or requests about your data can be sent through the project's repository.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We only use essential cookies: the Connect mode session and a temporary 10-minute one during sign-in. Your language preference may be kept in your browser.

Onboarding.title: Request your history from Spotify
Onboarding.lead: Encore uses the extended history, which Spotify emails you when you ask for it. It's free and covers everything since you created your account.
Onboarding.wait: Spotify may take up to 30 days to send it. It usually arrives sooner.

progress.title: Reading your history
progress.detail: {files, plural, =0 {Opening the file} one {# file read} other {# files read}} · {records, plural, =0 {no tracks yet} one {# track} other {# tracks}}

Upload.done: Done! {music, plural, one {# track read} other {# tracks read}} in {seconds} s, without leaving your device.

UNSUPPORTED_FILE.title: This file type isn't accepted
UNSUPPORTED_FILE.body: "{file}" is neither .zip nor .json. Upload the .zip Spotify sent you or the Streaming_History_Audio_*.json files.

INVALID_ZIP.title: I couldn't open this file
INVALID_ZIP.body: "{file}" doesn't look like a valid .zip. Upload the file Spotify emailed you, without unzipping it.

UNSAFE_PATH.title: Non-standard file
UNSAFE_PATH.body: For safety, we reject zips with suspicious paths (like "../"). Spotify's original .zip doesn't have them.

TOO_MANY_ENTRIES.title: File too large or non-standard
TOO_MANY_ENTRIES.body: The upload has more than {limit} files. Spotify's .zip usually has far fewer.

ENTRY_TOO_LARGE.title: File too large or non-standard
ENTRY_TOO_LARGE.body: "{entry}" is over {limit} MB unzipped. For safety, we reject files that large.

TOTAL_TOO_LARGE.title: File too large or non-standard
TOTAL_TOO_LARGE.body: For safety, we reject histories over {limit} MB unzipped.

COMPRESSION_RATIO.title: File too large or non-standard
COMPRESSION_RATIO.body: "{entry}" has a suspicious compression ratio (over {limit}×). For safety, we stopped reading.

NO_HISTORY_FILES.title: This zip doesn't have the extended history
NO_HISTORY_FILES.body: We looked for Streaming_History_Audio_*.json and found none. Check that it's the extended history file.

WRONG_EXPORT.title: This is the "Account data" package
WRONG_EXPORT.body: It only covers the last year, in a reduced format. Request the "Extended streaming history" to see everything.

INVALID_JSON.title: One of the files is corrupted
INVALID_JSON.body: "{entry}" isn't valid JSON. Download the .zip again from the link in Spotify's email.

UNEXPECTED_FORMAT.title: The format changed or this isn't a Spotify file
UNEXPECTED_FORMAT.body: "{entry}" doesn't have the fields we expect in a Spotify history.

INVALID_RECORDS.title: The format changed or the file is corrupted
INVALID_RECORDS.body: More than 5% of the records in "{entry}" ({invalid} of {total}) aren't in the expected format.

INTERNAL.title: The browser couldn't cope
INTERNAL.body: Something failed while reading the file, possibly low memory. Try on a computer or close other tabs.
